scope: Unapproved source correction proposal only; NOT ingested by enrichment normalization or generation.

existingValue.findingTextShort: Cannabidiol is a moderate CYP2C19 inhibitor.
existingValue.findingTextNormalized: Current EPIDIOLEX prescribing information identifies cannabidiol as a moderate CYP2C19 inhibitor and notes that concomitant use can increase plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates.

proposedValue.findingTextShort: EPIDIOLEX increases exposure to some CYP2C19 substrates but may decrease activation of prodrugs such as clopidogrel.
proposedValue.findingTextNormalized: The May 2026 EPIDIOLEX prescribing information identifies cannabidiol as a moderate CYP2C19 inhibitor. Concomitant EPIDIOLEX increases plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates. For substrates such as the prodrug clopidogrel, whose efficacy depends on active metabolites, concomitant EPIDIOLEX may decrease active-metabolite exposure and therefore may decrease efficacy. This is a prescription-label interaction warning, not a demonstrated clinical outcome for every nonprescription CBD formulation.

proposedCorrections.scientificRationale: The general substrate-exposure warning cannot be applied in the same direction to CYP2C19-activated prodrugs; the label expressly names clopidogrel and qualifies active-metabolite/efficacy reduction as a possibility.

existingValue.uncertaintyNote: Do not transfer this risk estimate to people with baseline liver disease, concomitant hepatotoxic medications, other doses, or longer durations without direct evidence.

proposedValue.uncertaintyNote: In this 28-day healthy-adult randomized trial, CBD 5 mg/kg/day was associated with ALT/AST elevations above 3 times the upper limit of normal in 5.6% of CBD participants versus 0% of placebo participants. This observation does not establish the molecular mechanism of liver injury. Do not transfer the trial-specific estimate to people with baseline liver disease, hepatotoxic co-medications, other CBD doses, or longer exposure without direct evidence.

proposedCorrections.scientificRationale: The randomized clinical observation is source-supported, but the publication does not establish a specific molecular or cellular mechanism behind the observed enzyme elevations. Severity and trial result remain unchanged.
